ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based customer due diligence under CMF Article L.561-5, including positive identification of politically exposed persons (PEPs) and members of the PEP's family/close associates. The diligence file must screen all UBOs, directors and authorized signatories against EU consolidated financial sanctions lists, UN Security Council sanctions, French asset-freeze measures administered by the Direction générale du Trésor, and, when USD rails or US correspondent banks are involved, OFAC sanctions. Screening must also cover negative news, adverse media, tax-evasion risk, and any link to goods subject to strategic/dual-use controls. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory because ISIC 5210 bond deposit in a free trade zone is a Medium_Risk_Enhanced activity; the engagement is refused or escalated if a matching designation, false UBO declaration, or unexplained shell-ownership pattern appears. Findings must be documented in writing and, where required, reported to TRACFIN.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique (www.guichet-entreprises.fr) operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI), using INPI legal availability data (data.inpi.fr) and Infogreffe commercial registry information
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French is the statutory language for all RCS entries, legal notices and administrative filings. A corporate name may include foreign words, but non-Latin script must be transliterated into Latin characters and the transliteration must be consistent across the articles, RCS application and publication. The chosen name must not be identical or confusingly similar to protected marks, natural persons' rights, or existing legal persons; registered RCS entries use Unicode UTF-8 with French diacritics.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon receipt of a rejection notice from the Guichet unique/registrar, the incorporator may, within 15 days, submit a written request for reconsideration to the same Guichet unique, attaching evidence of non-conflicting prior use, trademark search results, and the corrected name. If the rejection is maintained, the applicant may bring a summary enforcement application (référé) before the competent tribunal de commerce requesting that the registrar be ordered to accept the name and continue the incorporation; any administrative objection must be exhausted before the judicial référé. In parallel, the preferred expedient is to file a revised, non-conflicting name through the same portal, preserving the 30-day clearance window and avoiding delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A SAS may use an approved commercial domiciliation agent (domiciliataire agréé) for administrative registered-office purposes, but the French free-zone bonded warehouse operation itself requires a physical licensed customs depot; virtual or purely administrative offices cannot satisfy customs, excise, stock-control or supervisory substance requirements under the EU Customs Code.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Very high for bonded-depot operations: quantified likelihood of unannounced customs inspection is approximately 80–90% within the first 12 months of licensing, with near-certain initial pre-authorization physical inspection by the Direction générale des douanes et droits indirects (DGDDI). For a pure administrative domiciliation with no warehouse, the likelihood of on-site inspection of the registered office is materially lower, generally 10–20%.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.227-1 to L.227-30 (Société par Actions Simplifiée)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) operated by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce, through the INPI Guichet Unique
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts (Articles of Association) presiding with the Declaration of Subscription and Payment of Capital, filed via the INPI Guichet Unique
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: SAS has no legal minimum capital; capital must be fixed in the Statuts. Cash contributions must be fully subscribed at incorporation and at least 50% paid up upon signature, with the balance paid within 5 years. The paid-in amount must be deposited into a blocked bank account (compte bloqué) with a French bank or with the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations until the registration certificate (extrait Kbis) is issued.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The shareholders approve the subscription of the share capital set forth in the Statuts, acknowledging that each shareholder has paid up at least 50% of cash contributions, and certify that all funds have been deposited into the designated blocked account. (2) A registered office is fixed at [address] France. (3) The President of the SAS (and any General Manager) is appointed with powers to bind the company. (4) The President is authorized to complete all formalities with the RCS, customs authorities, and the relevant prefectures, and to take all necessary steps concerning the bonded depot operating permit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Corporate Document Preparation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Enter the desired corporate name into the INPI search portal to verify availability against RCS and INPI trademark records. Draft the Statuts, including share capital structure, registered office address, management rules, and the specific bonded warehouse operational purpose. This is the preparatory stage.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney for the designated filer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file a new name choice or appeal the INPI decision through the competent prefecture within established deadlines.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Blocked Capital Deposit and Bank Attestation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Approved French bank or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary blocked account in the name of the company in formation. Deposit the full subscription amount plus any agreed share premium. Obtain an attestation de blocage (blocking certificate) from the bank confirming the amount held, which must be submitted with the incorporation filing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the blocking certificate is incomplete, request a corrected attestation from the bank or apply for release and re-deposit if defects are material.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Dossier with Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the complete incorporation dossier through the official Guichet Unique website. The document set under French law is the M0 form, which includes the Statuts, bank block certificate, President’s consent, identity documents, and proof of the registered office address. The registry transmits the dossier to the RCS and extracts the Kbis upon validation.
required_dossiers: Declaration of beneficial ownership (BO – registre des bénéficiaires effectifs)
Identity and address proof of President and shareholders
Letter of the registered office owner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is rejected, correct the specified deficiencies within the sensible notice period and submit a revised dossier. For ex officio refusal, appeal to the presiding judge of the commercial court (Juge Commissaire) through the registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Public Notification in a Legal Gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d’Annonces Légales in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before or immediately after the filing, publish the required statutory notice of incorporation (including corporate name, registered office, capital amount, corporate purpose, and managers) in an authorized legal gazette of the relevant department. Submit proof of publication with the incorporation dossier.
required_dossiers: Proof of advertisement insertion (attestation de parution)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the publication is refused or the attestation is delayed, choose an alternative authorized gazette and resubmit until a valid attestation is obtained.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS Registration, Kbis Issuance, and Tax/Employment Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; Urssaf; DGFiP
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval of the incorporation dossier, the RCS registers the company and issues the extrait Kbis (official company extract). The Guichet Unique automatically coordinates registration with tax authorities (SIREN/NAF code), social security (Urssaf), and statistical authorities. For the bonded depot, the Kbis must be retained for filing customs license applications.
required_dossiers: Extrait Kbis of the registered company
Recorded corporate shareholder agreements if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Kbis is delayed, contact the registry and obtain a provisional certificate. If the assigned NAF code is incorrect, submit a change request through Guichet Unique with supporting evidence of the principal activity.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI) for customs/bonded warehouse status; Prefecture / DREAL for ICPE compliance
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d’entrepôt sous douane / Agrément d’entrepôt fiduciaire for a private or public customs warehouse within a free trade zone

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Direction Régionale de l’Environnement, de l’Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL) – France
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Regime of Enregistrement (subject to a detailed application file) under the French Environmental Code, typically ICPE Rubric 1510 for warehousing structures exceeding prevailing thresholds, with a full EIA required only when specific local contraints apply; otherwise classified under the Declaration regime with compliance notices
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the French Environment Code for fire water containment, minimal VOC emissions monitoring for any vehicle or machinery operations, limitations on wastewater discharge (non-hazardous neutral pH, no suspended solids above 350 mg/L without pre-treatment), assurance of separate storage of hazardous substances, and compliance with the municipal prefectural air quality and noise standards

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification (avis de la commission de sécurité) verifying compliance with French fire and rescue standards for logistics facilities; structural load inspection certificate issued by a qualified controller; occupational workplace clearance under the Labor Code (Code du travail) covering access, ergonomic, and emergency exit; compliance with the French insurance requirements for high-value bonded goods.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), official portal at impots.gouv.fr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: French-resident SAS entities obtain SIREN and SIRET via guichet-entreprises.fr or Chambre de Commerce et d'Industrie; VAT identification number (FR followed by 11 digits) is assigned automatically upon registration or upon exceeding the turnover threshold. Foreign entities must establish a French branch or subsidiary and register through the same channels.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box elections or hybrid mismatch elections are available in France; entity classification is fixed by law according to legal form and residency status. Domestic and EU rules on hybrid mismatches apply.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time electronic invoicing (facturation électronique) with digital time-stamping (horodatage) and transmission to DGFiP via certified providers; API integration required for clearance and digital stamping in bonded warehouse operations.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT rate applies to exports of goods outside the EU or to non-EU destinations and certain offshore services; eligibility requires proof of export and that the goods or services are not consumed in France or the EU.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration, Bill of Lading, Inward Remittance Certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Tax authorities perform rigorous audits on export claims; fraudulent zero-rating triggers penalties up to 80% of the evaded tax, interest charges, and potential criminal liability with retrospective clawback of benefits.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France is France's national central bank and part of the Eurosystem. The European Central Bank sets euro-area monetary policy. The French Treasury and the Directorate-General of Customs and Indirect Taxes (Direction générale des douanes et droits indirects, DGDDI) administer relevant financial and customs rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France applies the EU framework for free movement of capital and payments. The euro is freely convertible, and there is no general exchange-control approval requirement for a French SAS to receive foreign investment, pay overseas suppliers, or remit dividends, interest, or service fees. Remittances remain subject to corporate-law procedures, distributable-profit and solvency rules, withholding-tax requirements where applicable, treaty and EU-law conditions, transfer-pricing rules, bank AML checks, and sanctions screening. Cross-border payments may be subject to statistical reporting through financial institutions; French residents holding reportable accounts outside France may have separate tax-return disclosure obligations. Banks may request supporting documents and may delay or reject transactions that cannot be substantiated.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no general mandatory export-proceeds surrender, conversion ratio, or statutory conversion deadline. Export receipts may be retained in euros or foreign currency, subject to ordinary accounting, tax, sanctions, AML, and applicable statistical-reporting requirements. Customs export evidence and commercial records should be retained to support VAT and trade-finance treatment.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account; Capital Deposit Account for incorporation where offered
Operational Account; Capital Deposit Account for incorporation where offered

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole S.A. and the relevant regional caisse
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account; Capital Deposit Account subject to the selected entity's onboarding policy
Operational Account; Capital Deposit Account subject to local entity policy
Operational Account, subject to acceptance of the bonded-warehouse activity and international flows

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for ancillary payment services and foreign-currency collections; low as the sole treasury bank for a bonded-depot operator. Use only an EU-authorised credit institution or payment/e-money institution operating lawfully in France under its passport or local authorisation. Verify the provider and permissions in the applicable ACPR and EU registers. An EMI account is not a bank deposit and may not support capital deposits, customs guarantees, credit facilities, or commercial letters of credit. It does not remove French AML, sanctions, accounting, tax, or customs-documentation obligations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No general French law requires every director to attend a bank branch in person to open a corporate account. Remote onboarding may be available, but acceptance, identity verification, certified-document requirements, and interviews are bank-specific and risk-based. A bank may require an in-person meeting or additional verification for foreign directors, complex ownership, high-risk geographies, or unusual payment flows. Incorporation capital deposits and release procedures must follow the selected bank's process.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque ownership, nominee arrangements, or difficulty identifying natural-person ultimate beneficial owners.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current articles and registry extracts; ownership chart through each intermediate entity to natural-person beneficial owners; identity and address evidence; beneficial-owner filings; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence; board resolutions and authorised-signatory list.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign shareholder funding, large initial capital transfers, or payments inconsistent with the stated business plan.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Subscription and incorporation documents; shareholder and board resolutions; bank statements and traceable source-of-funds records; investment agreements; expected-flow schedule; counterparties, countries, currencies, and payment purposes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bonded or customs-controlled warehousing, unclear goods provenance, restricted goods, or mismatches between invoices, declarations, and payments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Applicable customs authorisations and warehouse approvals; customs-warehouse procedure and guarantee evidence; EORI registration; customer and supplier contracts; product and origin records; import/export declarations; transport and insurance documents; inventory controls; sanctions and restricted-goods screening procedures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume third-party payments, cash activity, unrelated payer/payee flows, or rapid movement of funds through the account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Documented funds-flow map; customer and supplier due-diligence files; invoices, purchase orders, bills of lading, warehouse receipts, and proof of delivery; reconciliation controls; cash-handling policy; transaction-monitoring and escalation procedures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions exposure, politically exposed persons, high-risk jurisdictions, or adverse media concerning owners, customers, suppliers, or goods.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Risk-based screening records; ownership and control checks; enhanced due-diligence files; documented assessment and approval; licences or competent-authority authorisations where legally required; evidence that prohibited dealings are blocked.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Receive shareholder funding into the SAS's French account from an account in the investor's own name or a clearly documented group account, using SEPA Credit Transfer for euro payments or SWIFT for other currencies. State the payment's true purpose, such as share capital subscription, share premium, shareholder loan, or intercompany financing; France does not prescribe a universal foreign-exchange purpose-code system. Provide the bank with subscription or loan documents, corporate approvals, beneficial-owner information, and source-of-funds evidence. For formation capital, follow the depositary bank's capital-deposit and release process. Record the transaction correctly in the company's accounts and complete applicable corporate, tax, statistical, and beneficial-owner formalities.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer where supported for eligible euro-area payments; use SWIFT MT103 or the bank's equivalent cross-border payment instruction for other currencies and destinations. Match each payment to an approved invoice, purchase order, contract, customs declaration, transport document, and warehouse or delivery evidence as applicable. For larger or higher-risk trades, use a documentary commercial letter of credit subject to agreed UCP 600 terms, documentary collection, or bank-guaranteed payment where commercially appropriate. Confirm beneficiary details independently, screen counterparties and banks, and reconcile fees, FX rates, and payment references. Customs duties, VAT, excise, and warehouse guarantees must be handled through the applicable customs and tax procedures, not treated as ordinary supplier payments.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with an authorised bank or appropriately authorised investment firm, supported by documented underlying exposure and applicable MiFID, EMIR, and reporting controls.
Non-deliverable forwards where commercially available and legally appropriate; confirm counterparty permissions, product classification, collateral terms, and reporting obligations.
Currency swaps and FX swaps with eligible counterparties, subject to documentation, valuation, collateral, EMIR clearing or reporting requirements where applicable, and internal counterparty limits.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual accounts and allocation of profit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders or sole shareholder of the SAS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Potential management liability and court injunction; failure to file approved accounts may trigger a EUR 1,500 fine, increased to EUR 3,000 for repeat non-compliance, and eventual administrative strike-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual accounts, management report where applicable, and related resolutions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent Commercial Court Registry through the French one-stop business portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval, or within two months where filed electronically
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: EUR 1,500 fine, increased to EUR 3,000 for repeat non-compliance; court injunction and possible administrative strike-off after formal notice and expiration of the applicable registry procedure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return Form 2065 and financial schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally by the second business day after 1 May for a calendar-year company; otherwise within three months after financial year-end, subject to the applicable electronic filing calendar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing interest at 0.20% per month and generally a 10% surcharge, increasing in cases of formal notice, repeated default, or tax assessment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent Commercial Court Registry through the French one-stop business portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No periodic annual filing; changes must generally be reported within 30 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court injunction, financial penalties, and potential criminal liability for failure to file or inaccurate beneficial ownership information; no automatic annual strike-off solely for absence of an annual confirmation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual local business tax compliance, including CFE payment and applicable declarations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual payment generally by 15 December; initial establishment and changes may require separate declarations by prescribed deadlines
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest and 5% surcharge generally apply, subject to statutory exceptions and tax administration procedures.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor is generally mandatory for a SAS exceeding at least two of the following thresholds for two consecutive financial years: EUR 5 million balance-sheet total, EUR 10 million net turnover, or 50 average employees. Appointment may also be required for specified controlled-company or group structures, or voluntarily by shareholder resolution.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP under the French Accounting Standards Authority (ANC) regulations for individual statutory accounts. IFRS may apply to qualifying consolidated accounts and may be used where legally permitted; it is not the default framework for individual SAS accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not generally require a separate annual beneficial ownership confirmation. The SAS must verify its ownership and control information annually as an internal compliance matter and file any change within 30 days. Share transfers must be reflected promptly in the securities movement register and individual shareholder accounts, with corresponding beneficial ownership updates where control changes.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of securities movements and individual shareholder accounts
Register or files of shareholder decisions and minutes
Register or files of decisions of the president and other corporate bodies where applicable
Beneficial ownership declaration records and supporting ownership documentation

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 650-2,200 per year, depending on address, mail handling, forwarding, and corporate secretarial services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 2,200-8,800 per year for a non-complex SAS; bonded warehousing, customs controls, inventory systems, or group reporting may increase the fee

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: R&D tax credit (30% of eligible expenses), innovation status (15% CIT rate for qualifying innovative firms for 5 years), tax loss carryforward

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 1200-A (Déclaration de résultat) filed electronically via impots.gouv.fr
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 3 months after fiscal year-end (e.g., 31 March for 31 December year-end)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate income and expenses prior to tax adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: French SAS reports French and worldwide income; non-residents limited to French-source income absent permanent establishment
Apply transfer pricing adjustments and deductions; non-residents invoke treaty benefits via TRC submission

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties €750 per month (capped at 80% of tax due); criminal sanctions including imprisonment for evasion

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Submit Treaty Relief Certificate (TRC) to French tax authorities with withholding declaration to apply reduced DTA rate
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0%–25% (standard 10% under most treaties); Interest: 0%–10% (often 0% for portfolio interest)

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Economic Substance Regulations apply to high-risk activities (IP holding, finance); bonded warehouse operations generally exempt

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of income or false CIT declarations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to 80% of evaded tax plus imprisonment up to 5 years and full restitution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal criminal liability including imprisonment; corporate veil may be pierced

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to File or Late Filing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines €750 per month of delay (capped at 80% of tax due)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for penalties; potential disqualification from office

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Absence of arm's length documentation or use of non-approved methodologies
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment plus penalties up to 80% of adjustment plus interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability for fraudulent TP schemes; possible imprisonment

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Misuse of Free Trade Zone / Bonded Warehouse Benefits
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: False declarations of goods or improper exemption claims
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Customs fines, CIT penalties, and potential criminal prosecution for fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal fines and imprisonment for willful misconduct
